Clean white backgrounds, fully clothed varied adults, charcoal-gray clothing/equipment with lime accent, anatomically correct, physically plausible supports. No lettering/logos/watermarks. Whole figure and apparatus entirely inside own panel, generous margins. Render each POSITIVE VISUAL DESCRIPTION precisely. Avoid default generic fitness poses; geometry and hand directions are essential. 

Row 1 column 1: Supine adult on FLOOR. One dumbbell across PELVIS held with hands. SOLES OF BOTH SHOES TOUCH each other, heel-to-heel and toe-to-toe forming diamond, knees opened OUTWARD. Hips raised in frog glute bridge. Entire back/neck supported floor. Equipment is only ONE dumbbell.

Row 1 column 2: Adult lies FACE DOWN on flat bench. Non-working hand under forehead. Working upper arm extends SIDEWAYS horizontally at SHOULDER HEIGHT; elbow bent90 and forearm points forward parallel floor holding ONE dumbbell. Working elbow stays level with shoulder. Row 2 column 1: Two supinated dumbbells, athlete hinged at hips with back exactly HORIZONTAL, flat back, knees bent slightly. Both elbows pulled toward hips, weights near lower ribs. Strong full side view to show horizontal torso.

Row 2 column 2: Athlete front view: LEFT elbow bent90 glued to left waist, LEFT forearm pointing to left/outward. Band crosses front abdomen from LEFT working hand to rack anchor on RIGHT side of image/body. Band tension pulls forearm INWARD; athlete rotates OUTWARD. Elbow remains90.

cells.title: Dumbbell Lying Pronation
cells.guideText:
Lie on a flat bench face down with one arm holding a dumbbell and the other hand on top of the bench folded so that you can rest your head on it.

Bend the elbows of the arm holding the dumbbell so that it creates a 90-degree angle between the upper arm and the forearm.

Now raise the upper arm so that the forearm is perpendicular to the floor and the upper arm is perpendicular to your torso. Tip: The upper arm should be parallel to the floor and also creating a 90-degree angle with your torso. This will be your starting position.

As you breathe out, externally rotate your forearm so that the dumbbell is lifted forward as you maintain the 90 degree angle bend between the upper arms and the forearm. You will continue this external rotation until the forearm is parallel to the floor. At this point you will hold the contraction for a second.

As you breathe in, slowly go back to the starting position.

Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

cells.title: Dumbbell Underhand Dead Row
cells.guideText: The Dumbbell Underhand Dead Row will involve the back, which means you can try a bit heavier weight. The catch is that you need to be able to control the weight for all the reps. 1. Start by holding a pair of dumbbells with your feet shoulder-wide apart and your knees slightly bent. 2. Hinge at your hips to lower your torse forward until it's almost parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat and maintaining a slight bend in your knees. 3. Exhale as you row the dumbbells to your sides up to chest height, leading with your elbows until your upper arms are just past parallel to the floor and the dumbbells are at ribcage level. 4. Slowly lower to the starting position and repeat. Keep your back flat all the time.

cells.title: Band external rotation
cells.guideText:
Choke the band around a post. The band should be at the same height as your elbow. Stand with your left side to the band a couple of feet away.

Grasp the end of the band with your right hand, and keep your elbow pressed firmly to your side. We recommend you hold a pad or foam roll in place with your elbow to keep it firmly in position.

With your upper arm in position, your elbow should be flexed to 90 degrees with your hand reaching across the front of your torso. This will be your starting position.

Execute the movement by rotating your arm in a backhand motion, keeping your elbow in place.

Continue as far as you are able, pause, and then return to the starting position.
